Here is a summary of the article:

The UK government spent £3.4 billion on private consultants in 2023-24, representing a 62% increase from pre-pandemic levels in 2019-20. Despite the pandemic ending, consultant spending remains elevated and has not returned to previous baselines. This poses a significant challenge for Prime Minister Keir Starmer's administration, which has pledged to reduce consultant spending by half during the current parliament. Since Labour took office, approximately £650 million in new consultant contracts have been awarded, including a £223 million deal with KPMG to train civil servants over 15 months. Labour peer Prem Sikka criticized the practice, describing it as part of a problematic culture of hiring consultants who cannot meaningfully understand complex organizations in short time periods.
